## Review protocol
# Review protocol for outside AI agents (Argon, Gemini, ChatGPT, others)

Outside reviews keep coming back half-read or made up. These rules are mandatory. A review that skips them gets thrown out.

## 1. Prove you read it
- Open files in raw view: `https://github.com/rcbailey12/voidsworn/raw/main/<path>`. Not the normal GitHub page (it folds long lines and loads in chunks).
- Write down the commit you reviewed (the short id shown on the repo's main page).
- For every file: total line count, and the exact text of the first 40 characters of the LAST line.
- Big files (over 1,500 lines or 60 KB): read in parts by line range and list each range you read. Never assume the rest.
- If you cannot see the end of a file, stop and say so.

## 2. Stay in scope
- Answer only the question you were given, on only the files named. No general advice ("consider adding tests").
- Max 10 findings, most important first. Fewer good findings beat many weak ones.

## 3. Evidence for every claim
- Each finding: file, line number, and an exact quote (under 20 words) copied from the file.
- Every function, variable or setting you name must appear in the file. Search for it before you write it. Do not invent names or APIs.
- Mark each finding OBSERVED (you saw it in the code) or INFERRED (your reasoning). Inferred findings need a reason.
- "Not enough info" is a good answer. Guessing is not.

## 4. Check yourself before you hand it in
- Re-open every cited line and confirm the quote matches word for word. Delete any finding whose quote does not match.
- End with "Not checked": what you did not read or could not verify.

## 5. Output
- Table: # | finding | OBSERVED/INFERRED | file:line | exact quote | why it matters | your fix | confidence (high/med/low)
- Then your one recommended next step.
- Save it as `contrib/<your-name>/reviews/<topic>.md`. Do not edit any file outside `contrib/`.

## Tips for whoever starts the review
- Gemini: uploading the files directly (it takes very long inputs) is more reliable than letting it browse.
- One system per run (battle rules, then AI, then menus...), not "the whole game".
- Paste this file's rules into the prompt, or tell the agent: "Follow docs/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md exactly."
- Claude checks every claim against the code before merging anything (see docs/ship_pipeline/AUDIT_SYNTHESIS.md).

# the largest scale (at most 1) that keeps every outline point, turned by `bearing` about the vertical, inside the cells
# (positions relative to the station's centre)
static func fit_scale(points: PackedVector2Array, cells: Array, hex_r: float, bearing: float) -> float:
	var rays := footprint_rays(cells, hex_r)
	var k := 1.0
	var basis := Basis.from_euler(Vector3(0, bearing, 0))
	for p in points:
		var v := basis * Vector3(p.x, 0, p.y)
		var q := Vector2(v.x, v.z)
		var r := q.length()
		if r < 1e-4:
			continue
		var f := fposmod(q.angle() / TAU, 1.0) * FIT_ANGLES
		var i0 := int(floor(f)) % FIT_ANGLES
		var d := minf(rays[i0], rays[(i0 + 1) % FIT_ANGLES])
		k = minf(k, d / r)
	return k * 0.98   # a hair inside the edge


# The turn, from `bearing` plus a multiple of TAU / FIT_TURNS, whose fit_scale is largest, as Vector2(bearing, scale). The
# outline points are binned once by angle at the rays' own resolution, keeping each bin's farthest point; a turn by a whole
# number of bins moves every point by whole rays, so each candidate's scale is the same as fit_scale's (no second pass).
# Ties keep the drawn bearing first.
const FIT_TURNS := 24
static func best_bearing(points: PackedVector2Array, cells: Array, hex_r: float, bearing: float) -> Vector2:
	var rays := footprint_rays(cells, hex_r)
	var far := PackedFloat32Array()
	far.resize(FIT_ANGLES)
	var basis := Basis.from_euler(Vector3(0, bearing, 0))
	for p in points:
		var v := basis * Vector3(p.x, 0, p.y)
		var q := Vector2(v.x, v.z)
		var r := q.length()
		if r < 1e-4:
			continue
		var i0 := int(floor(fposmod(q.angle() / TAU, 1.0) * FIT_ANGLES)) % FIT_ANGLES
		far[i0] = maxf(far[i0], r)
	var step := FIT_ANGLES / FIT_TURNS
	var best := Vector2(bearing, -1.0)
	for j in FIT_TURNS:
		var k := 1.0
		for i in FIT_ANGLES:
			if far[i] <= 0.0:
				continue
			# a turn of j * TAU / FIT_TURNS more lowers every point's angle by j * step rays
			var a := posmod(i - j * step, FIT_ANGLES)
			k = minf(k, minf(rays[a], rays[(a + 1) % FIT_ANGLES]) / far[i])
		if k * 0.98 > best.y + 1e-6:
			best = Vector2(bearing + TAU * float(j) / float(FIT_TURNS), k * 0.98)
	return best


# The painted station across a cluster of station hexes. `kind` is the biome's station kind, `with_debris` false for a lone
# blocker hex (its torn pieces would drift over open hexes). `cells` are the cluster's hex centres relative to the station
# centre (x, z), `hex_r` their corner radius and `bearing` the turn the caller will give it: when `cells` is set and the
# cluster is smaller than the big station, T2 is fitted inside them.
static func station(size: float, debris_clearance := 0.0, kind := "", with_debris := true, cells: Array = [], hex_r := 10.0, bearing := 0.0) -> Node3D:
	if old_path():
		if size != LARGE_STATION_SIZE:
			return _o1(size, "")
		kind = ""
	var info: Dictionary = STATION_KINDS.get(kind, {})
	var path := T2_PATH
	if info.has("scene") and ResourceLoader.exists(str(info["scene"])):
		path = str(info["scene"])
	if ResourceLoader.exists(path):
		var t2 := (load(path) as PackedScene).instantiate() as Node3D
		t2.set_meta("station_T2", true)
		t2.set_meta("station_kind", kind)
		if not _reach.has(path):
			_outline[path] = outline_points(t2)
			var far := 0.0
			for q in _outline[path]:
				far = maxf(far, (q as Vector2).length())
			_reach[path] = far if far > 0.0 else T2_REACH
		var k := 1.0
		# only the approved big 19-hex station keeps unit scale; any other cluster that names its cells is fitted (a 5 to
		# 18 hex cluster too: Fable on PR 1772, L2)
		var fit := cells.size() < BIG_FOOTPRINT_CELLS if not cells.is_empty() else size < LARGE_STATION_SIZE
		if fit:
			if not cells.is_empty() and not (_outline[path] as PackedVector2Array).is_empty():
				# Wave 0 on Sheet M (Fable, Astra, Neon, Nov 23): a fitted T2 read small and left the teaching cluster's
				# outer hexes empty, so it is turned to the best of FIT_TURNS bearings from the drawn one (the largest
				# exact fit); the caller turns it by the "station_bearing" this records
				var best := best_bearing(_outline[path], cells, hex_r, bearing)
				bearing = best.x
				k = minf(1.0, best.y)
			else:
				k = clampf(size / LARGE_STATION_SIZE, 0.05, 1.0)
		t2.scale = Vector3.ONE * k
		t2.set_meta("station_scale", k)
		t2.set_meta("station_bearing", bearing)
		# Refs #863. Separate kit/cache leaves PR 977's painted station intact. The field lives in T2's own (scaled) frame,
		# so the clearance it keeps out of is divided by the same scale.
		if with_debris and path == T2_PATH and ResourceLoader.exists(T2_DEBRIS_PATH):
			var debris := (load(T2_DEBRIS_PATH) as PackedScene).instantiate() as Node3D
			debris.name = "station_T2_debris"
			debris.set_script(load("res://render/station_debris.gd"))
			t2.add_child(debris)
			debris.keep_outside(debris_clearance / k)
		var look = load("res://render/look.gd")
		var painted := {}
		for child in t2.find_children("*", "MeshInstance3D", true, false):
			for i in child.mesh.get_surface_count():
				var source: Material = child.get_active_material(i)
				if not painted.has(source):
					painted[source] = look.hull(source, "hegemony", true)
				child.set_surface_override_material(i, painted[source])
		for player in t2.find_children("*", "AnimationPlayer", true, false):
			var names: PackedStringArray = player.get_animation_list()
			for anim in names:
				if anim != "RESET":
					player.get_animation(anim).loop_mode = Animation.LOOP_LINEAR
					player.play(anim)
					break
		if info.has("light"):
			# one faint unshadowed lamp inside the station's own reach, in the kind's colour (light on nearby hulls stays faint, 6.8)
			var lamp := OmniLight3D.new()
			lamp.name = "station_kind_light"
			lamp.light_color = info["light"]
			lamp.light_energy = KIND_LIGHT_ENERGY
			lamp.omni_range = float(_reach[path]) * 0.5 * k
			lamp.scale = Vector3.ONE / k   # world range = the line above, whether or not the engine scales light range
			lamp.shadow_enabled = false
			lamp.position = Vector3(0, 6.0, 0)
			t2.add_child(lamp)
		return t2
	return _o1(size, kind)


# the old normalized O1_37 at `size` (the fallback when T2 is not built)
static func _o1(size: float, kind: String) -> Node3D:
	var n := _scene("O1_37")
	if n == null:
		return null
	var root := Node3D.new()
	root.name = "station"
	root.set_meta("station_kind", kind)
	n.scale = Vector3.ONE * size  # A4 ships are about 1.0 long (+X), so the scale is the size
	root.add_child(n)
	return root


# Issue 1536 (Ryan, Nov 22 2026: "Yes" to showing the Relay in Hold battles): the Navy relay beacon O3_11 for the hold hex, in
# the Navy finish (render/look.gd, as the station), scaled so its length along x is `length`, centred on its own box. Null when
# the build has no O3_11 (the board then keeps its gold hex alone).
static func beacon(length: float) -> Node3D:
	var n := _scene(BEACON_CODE)
	if n == null:
		return null
	var look = load("res://render/look.gd")
	var painted := {}
	var box := AABB()
	var first := true
	for child in n.find_children("*", "MeshInstance3D", true, false):
		var mi := child as MeshInstance3D
		if mi.mesh == null:
			continue
		for i in mi.mesh.get_surface_count():
			var source: Material = mi.get_active_material(i)
			if source != null and not painted.has(source):
				painted[source] = look.hull(source, "hegemony", true)
			if source != null:
				mi.set_surface_override_material(i, painted[source])
		var xf := Transform3D.IDENTITY
		var p: Node = mi
		while p != null and p != n:
			xf = (p as Node3D).transform * xf if p is Node3D else xf
			p = p.get_parent()
		var bb := xf * mi.get_aabb()
		box = bb if first else box.merge(bb)
		first = false
	var root := Node3D.new()
	root.name = "relay_beacon"
	var k := length / maxf(box.size.x, 1e-3)
	n.scale = Vector3.ONE * k
	n.position = -box.get_center() * k
	root.add_child(n)
	return root


# Issue 1767 (R419): the derelict hulls a map's hulk hexes draw from, one or two per faction, all six factions (before
# this only the Directorate, Crusade, Hullbreakers and Eclipse ever appeared). Destroyers and cruisers, true chirality.
const HULKS := {
	"hegemony": ["H8_23"],
	"voidsworn": ["V15_37"],
	"corsair": ["C14s_23"],
	"deathless": ["D20_23"],
	"chorus": ["B20_11", "B21_11"],
	"ithar": ["I11_37", "I15_11"],
}
const HULK_LOCAL_PCT := 70   # percent of hulks drawn from the factions in the battle, the rest from any faction


static func hulk_faction(code: String) -> String:
	for fac in HULKS:
		if code in HULKS[fac]:
			return fac
	return ""


# one hulk code from one random draw `v` (so the board keeps its old number of draws): HULK_LOCAL_PCT of the time a hull of
# a faction in `local` (the battle's factions), else any faction's
static func pick_hulk(v: int, local: Array = []) -> String:
	v = absi(v)
	if old_path():
		return OLD_HULKS[v % OLD_HULKS.size()]
	# the faction first, then one of its hulls, so a faction with two hulls is drawn no more often (Fable on PR 1772, L2)
	var every: Array = HULKS.keys()
	var near: Array = every.filter(func(f): return f in local)
	var pool: Array = near if not near.is_empty() and v % 100 < HULK_LOCAL_PCT else every
	var rest := v / 100
	var codes: Array = HULKS[pool[rest % pool.size()]]
	return str(codes[(rest / pool.size()) % codes.size()])


# a derelict: the A4 hull in its own paint, burnt (darker, rougher, its windows and engines dead), unit length: scale it as the
# board scales its hulks. The burn suits the material (R416, R420 Law 3): the paint is dimmed and pulled toward the
# faction's own scorch colour by its wreck_soot, so Chorus chitin and Glasswright glass (wreck_soot 0) keep their own
# hue and gloss and Eclipse keeps its violet-black (never the old shared warm soot), then held in the dull band.
static func hulk(code: String) -> Node3D:
	var n := _scene(code)
	if n == null:
		return null
	var fac := hulk_faction(code)
	n.set_meta("hulk_faction", fac)
	for mi in n.find_children("*", "MeshInstance3D", true, false):
		var m := mi as MeshInstance3D
		if m.mesh == null:
			continue
		for i in m.mesh.get_surface_count():
			var src := m.get_active_material(i) as BaseMaterial3D
			if src == null:
				continue
			m.set_surface_override_material(i, derelict_shared(src, fac))
	return n


# PR 1772 LOAD probe (Board, Nov 22): a graveyard reuses one burnt copy per source material and faction, so 31 hulks of
# 8 hulls make one material per hull surface, not one per hulk surface. Nothing changes a hulk's material afterwards.
# The cache owns nothing: each entry holds weak references to its source and to the burnt copy, so the copies live only
# as long as the hulks wearing them. When a battle ends (to the map, or into a battle with no hulks) they go with the
# board, and dead entries are dropped on the next lookup (Antigravity audit and Artoo on PR 1772, Nov 23).
static var _derelict_cache := {}   # key -> [weakref(source material), weakref(burnt copy)]
static func derelict_shared(src: BaseMaterial3D, fac: String) -> BaseMaterial3D:
	var key := "%d|%s|%s" % [src.get_instance_id(), fac, old_path()]
	var hit = _derelict_cache.get(key)
	if hit != null and (hit[0] as WeakRef).get_ref() == src:
		var live = (hit[1] as WeakRef).get_ref()
		if live != null:
			return live
	for k in _derelict_cache.keys():
		if (_derelict_cache[k][0] as WeakRef).get_ref() == null or (_derelict_cache[k][1] as WeakRef).get_ref() == null:
			_derelict_cache.erase(k)
	var made := derelict(src, fac)
	_derelict_cache[key] = [weakref(src), weakref(made)]
	return made



# R420 Law 1 band 3 (contrib/opus/plans/global_cohesion_standard.md): a lit hulk is a dead hull, so its effective base
# albedo (paint texture times tint) is its own paint dimmed (DEAD_DIM, then the faction's burn) and held under a dull
# ceiling, 0.045 linear, so no faction's derelict (the Glasswrights' pale glass above all: Fable on PR 1772, H9) is the
# brightest thing in a graveyard. The ceiling was 0.12 until the PROPS_E pictures (Nov 22 2026), then 0.07 until PROPS_G.
# R425 (Ryan, Nov 23 2026): a wreck is never lighter than its dimmed live paint; the floor only stops pure black. The
# 0.04 floor (and R423's 0.025 for Chorus) had lifted dark paint back up: the Chorus body (about 0.021 live) rendered
# undimmed and the Hullbreaker hull went from 0.027 live to 0.040 dead (CHORUSMAT probe, PR 1772).
const HULK_BAND := Vector2(0.005, 0.045)
# R423 (Ryan, Nov 23 2026): Chorus hulks sit lower still, the tan chitin wrecks under a 0.03 ceiling (PROPS_I).
const CHORUS_HULK_BAND := Vector2(0.005, 0.03)
# Eclipse obsidian keeps the floor it was approved on (R421, unchanged by R425): about 0.04
const OBSIDIAN_BAND := Vector2(0.04, 0.045)
# Visible burn: scorch patches multiplied over the hull's own UVs, their share of the hull growing with wreck_soot
# (Hullbreakers most, Navy least); a faction with wreck_soot 0 (Chorus, Glasswrights) and Eclipse obsidian get none.
const BURN_EDGE := Vector2(0.4, 0.35)  # ramp edge = x + y * wreck_soot: the burnt share of the noise (heavier after PROPS_G)
const BURN_DARK := 2.5                 # the patch multiplier is the faction's scorch colour times this, capped at 1
const BURN_FREQ := 0.012               # about three patches across the hull's UV square
static var _burn_cache := {}
const DEAD_DIM := 0.6   # a dead hull with no lights: its paint dimmed before any soot
const OBSIDIAN := Color(0.22, 0.19, 0.28)   # an Eclipse hulk's effective albedo: violet-black obsidian (R420 Law 3)
const OBSIDIAN_ROUGH := 0.3                 # obsidian keeps a glassy sheen
const CHITIN_DRY_ROUGH := 0.85
const DEAD_METAL_DIM := 0.4    # dead metal (wreck_soot above 0) keeps at most this share of its paint before the band
const DEAD_METAL_KEEP := 0.5   # and this share of its metalness
const DEAD_SPECULAR := 0.2     # and at most this dielectric sheen (Godot's default is 0.5)
const DEAD_GLASS_SPEC := 0.6   # Glasswright dead glass: its sheen times this, gloss kept              # a dead Chorus hull is dry, matte chitin
# The burn comes from the faction's own wound profile (fx/faction_looks.json "wound": scorch_col, wreck_soot; PR 1755,
# issue 1741), the one home for how a faction's hull scorches. Until that block is on main these are its values.
const WOUND_FALLBACK := {
	"voidsworn": {"scorch_col": [0.1, 0.08, 0.07], "wreck_soot": 0.55},
	"hegemony": {"scorch_col": [0.16, 0.18, 0.22], "wreck_soot": 0.25},
	"corsair": {"scorch_col": [0.09, 0.06, 0.045], "wreck_soot": 0.7},
	"chorus": {"scorch_col": [0.2, 0.13, 0.07], "wreck_soot": 0.0},
	"ithar": {"scorch_col": [0.8, 0.86, 0.95], "wreck_soot": 0.0},
	"deathless": {"scorch_col": [0.1, 0.07, 0.14], "wreck_soot": 0.15},
}
static var _tex_mean := {}   # not GPU: albedo texture resource path or id -> its mean colour


static func wound_of(fac: String) -> Dictionary:
	var w = load("res://fx/faction_look.gd").of(fac).get("wound", {}) if fac != "" else {}
	if not (w is Dictionary) or not (w as Dictionary).has("wreck_soot"):
		w = WOUND_FALLBACK.get(fac, WOUND_FALLBACK["voidsworn"])
	return w


# the mean colour of a material's albedo texture (white when it has none), cached per texture. Artoo on PR 1772: only a
# small mip is decompressed and averaged (a 4 x 4 to 8 x 8 level, 16 to 64 pixels), never the whole map; a texture
# without mips is averaged from a nearest-sampled 16 x 16 copy.
static func texture_mean(m: BaseMaterial3D) -> Color:
	var t := m.albedo_texture
	if t == null:
		return Color.WHITE
	var key: String = t.resource_path if t.resource_path != "" else str(t.get_instance_id())
	if _tex_mean.has(key):
		return _tex_mean[key]
	var out := Color.WHITE
	var img := t.get_image()
	if img != null and not img.is_empty():
		out = image_mean(img)
	_tex_mean[key] = out
	return out


static func image_mean(img: Image) -> Color:
	var small: Image = null
	if img.has_mipmaps():
		var w := img.get_width()
		var h := img.get_height()
		var count := img.get_mipmap_count()
		var level := 0
		for l in range(count + 1):
			if maxi(1, w >> l) >= 4 and maxi(1, h >> l) >= 4:
				level = l
		var data := img.get_data()
		var start := img.get_mipmap_offset(level) if level > 0 else 0
		var end := img.get_mipmap_offset(level + 1) if level < count else data.size()
		small = Image.create_from_data(maxi(1, w >> level), maxi(1, h >> level), false, img.get_format(), data.slice(start, end))
	else:
		small = img.duplicate() as Image
		if small.is_compressed():
			small.decompress()
		small.resize(16, 16, Image.INTERPOLATE_NEAREST)
	if small.is_compressed():
		small.decompress()
	small.convert(Image.FORMAT_RGBAF)
	var acc := Color(0, 0, 0, 0)
	for y in small.get_height():
		for x in small.get_width():
			acc += small.get_pixel(x, y)
	var n := float(small.get_width() * small.get_height())
	return Color(acc.r / n, acc.g / n, acc.b / n, acc.a / n)


static func linear_luma(c: Color) -> float:
	var l := c.srgb_to_linear()
	return 0.2126 * l.r + 0.7152 * l.g + 0.0722 * l.b


# the luminance the shader actually lights: texture and tint each decoded to linear, then multiplied (Artoo on PR 1772 at
# deddb79b: multiplying the encoded values first measured one space and corrected in another)
static func effective_luma(mean: Color, tint: Color) -> float:
	var m := mean.srgb_to_linear()
	var t := tint.srgb_to_linear()
	return 0.2126 * m.r * t.r + 0.7152 * m.g * t.g + 0.0722 * m.b * t.b


# scale a tint (same hue and alpha) so the effective albedo, linear texture times linear tint, lies inside the band
static func into_band(c: Color, mean := Color.WHITE, band := HULK_BAND) -> Color:
	var y := effective_luma(mean, c)
	if y <= 1e-5:
		return c
	var want := clampf(y, band.x, band.y)
	if is_equal_approx(want, y):
		return c
	var l := c.srgb_to_linear()
	var k := want / y
	var out := Color(minf(l.r * k, 1.0), minf(l.g * k, 1.0), minf(l.b * k, 1.0), 1.0).linear_to_srgb()
	out.a = c.a
	return out


# the burnt copy of one hull material for a faction's derelict
static func derelict(src: BaseMaterial3D, fac: String) -> BaseMaterial3D:
	var b := src.duplicate() as BaseMaterial3D
	b.emission_enabled = false
	if old_path():
		b.albedo_color = Color(0.32, 0.29, 0.27)  # the old shared soot (VS_1767_OLD before pictures only)
		b.roughness = minf(1.0, b.roughness * 1.2)
		return b
	var w := wound_of(fac)
	var soot := clampf(float(w.get("wreck_soot", 0.0)), 0.0, 1.0)
	var sc: Array = w.get("scorch_col", [0.1, 0.1, 0.1])
	var c := src.albedo_color
	var mean := texture_mean(src)
	if fac == "deathless":
		# Ryan, Nov 22 2026 (Astra's cleanup, item 4): an Eclipse hulk is dark obsidian, violet-black and glossy, never a
		# dimmed paint that reads brown; the tint is solved so paint times tint lands on OBSIDIAN, then held in the band
		var t := Color(minf(1.0, OBSIDIAN.r / maxf(mean.r, 0.02)), minf(1.0, OBSIDIAN.g / maxf(mean.g, 0.02)),
			minf(1.0, OBSIDIAN.b / maxf(mean.b, 0.02)), c.a)
		# held to the exact tint Ryan approved on PROPS_E (R421): its band step keeps the encoded-space measure it was
		# approved with, so the linear-space fix below (Artoo at deddb79b) leaves the Eclipse look unchanged
		var ye := linear_luma(Color(mean.r * t.r, mean.g * t.g, mean.b * t.b))
		var we := clampf(ye, OBSIDIAN_BAND.x, OBSIDIAN_BAND.y)
		if ye > 1e-5 and not is_equal_approx(we, ye):
			var lt := t.srgb_to_linear()
			var ke := we / ye
			t = Color(minf(lt.r * ke, 1.0), minf(lt.g * ke, 1.0), minf(lt.b * ke, 1.0), 1.0).linear_to_srgb()
			t.a = c.a
		b.albedo_color = t
		b.roughness = minf(src.roughness, OBSIDIAN_ROUGH)
		return b
	var burn := Color(DEAD_DIM, DEAD_DIM, DEAD_DIM).lerp(Color(float(sc[0]), float(sc[1]), float(sc[2])), soot)
	if soot > 0.0:
		# dead metal keeps at most DEAD_METAL_DIM of its paint's light (Wave 0 on Sheet M, Nov 23: Fable, Astra and Neon saw
		# the Directorate wrecks read silver-white at c170; their pale blue-grey scorch at the lightest soot left them at
		# about half their paint). Darker only, so it stays inside R425 (never lighter than 60% of live paint; the floor
		# only stops pure black); Hullbreakers and Sunward already sit under it.
		burn = Color(minf(burn.r, DEAD_METAL_DIM), minf(burn.g, DEAD_METAL_DIM), minf(burn.b, DEAD_METAL_DIM))
	b.albedo_color = into_band(Color(c.r * burn.r, c.g * burn.g, c.b * burn.b, c.a), mean,
		CHORUS_HULK_BAND if fac == "chorus" else HULK_BAND)
	b.roughness = minf(1.0, src.roughness * (1.0 + 0.35 * soot))   # soot dulls metal; glass and chitin keep their gloss
	if fac == "chorus":
		# dead chitin dries out (Board on PROPS_H, Nov 23: the Chorus wrecks still pop in the field). Its albedo already sits
		# on the band 3 floor (R420: 0.04 linear is the floor for hulks), so the wet sheen goes instead of more darkening.
		b.roughness = maxf(b.roughness, CHITIN_DRY_ROUGH)
	if soot > 0.0:
		# a dead metal hull loses its polish: half its metal and a dull dielectric sheen, so the sky no longer paints a
		# silver gleam on it at the battle camera (the same Wave 0 finding; its roughness map is kept)
		b.metallic = src.metallic * DEAD_METAL_KEEP
		b.metallic_specular = minf(src.metallic_specular, DEAD_SPECULAR)
	elif fac == "ithar":
		# dead glass keeps its clarity and gloss (roughness untouched) but its lights are out, so its glints soften

	while Engine.get_process_frames() < target:
		await get_tree().process_frame

func _step() -> void:
	_settle()
	fx.step(STEP)
	if wld != null and is_instance_valid(wld) and wld.has_method("step"):
		wld.step(STEP)
	steps += 1
	if headless:
		await get_tree().process_frame   # no draw signal without a renderer (the cloud smoke run)
	else:
		await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw


# every worker job (hull damage rebuilds, death cuts) finished before the clock moves (scene_gate.gd _settle)
func _settle() -> void:
	for id in fx.ships:
		var sh = fx.ships[id]
		if int(sh._dmg_task) >= 0:
			_wait_task(int(sh._dmg_task), "hull damage rebuild", id)
		if sh.has_meta("cut_task"):
			_wait_task(int(sh.get_meta("cut_task")), "death cut", id)


# issue 1236 (WRECK1 sat 25 minutes with no log): a worker job that keeps the clock waiting names its ship and kind, at
# 5, 10, 20 s and so on; nothing is printed while jobs finish in time (Artoo on PR 1785: the damage wait logs too)
func _wait_task(task: int, kind: String, id) -> void:
	var t0 := Time.get_ticks_msec()
	var told := 5000
	while not WorkerThreadPool.is_task_completed(task):
		OS.delay_usec(300)
		if Time.get_ticks_msec() - t0 > told:
			_log("settle: %s's %s still running after %d s" % [str(id), kind, told / 1000])
			told *= 2


func _clear() -> void:
	for id in fx.ships.keys():
		fx.remove_ship(str(id))
		if fx.has_method("clear_wreck"):
			fx.clear_wreck(str(id))
	for n in world.get_children():
		if n is Node3D and String(n.name).begins_with("ship_"):
			world.remove_child(n)
			n.queue_free()
	A = null
	T = null

func _ship(id: String, fac: String, cls: String, pos: Vector3, facing: int, code := ""):
	var sv = SV.new()

	world.add_child(sv)

	if code != "":
		u["code"] = code
		u["L"] = float(OBJ_LEN.get(code, 10.0))
	sv.setup(u, pos, true)
	sv.set_process(false)   # its bob and idle jets run on the wall clock (see the header)
	if _is_block(sv) and not args.has("allow-blocks"):
		_placeholder("%s %s drew a block (code %s)" % [fac, cls, str(sv.code)])
		return null

	if not sv.a4:
		info["meshes"] = sv.meshes
	fx.add_ship(id, sv, info)
	sv.fx_engines = true
	fx.set_engine(id, 0.3)
	fx.sync_ship(id, _unit(1.0, 5))
	return sv

func _hits(n: int, shield: bool, crit: bool) -> Array:

func _moment(row: Dictionary, r: float, crop: Vector2i, cell: Vector2i, d: String, keep := true) -> bool:
	var id := str(row["id"])
	_clear()
	_make_fx()
	# Issue 462: a row may set effect switches (for example reduce flashing). Set by
	# name so a commit without the switch simply ignores it.
	var opts = row.get("fx", {})
	if opts is Dictionary:
		for k in opts:
			fx.set(str(k), opts[k])
	_cam(Vector3.ZERO, r)
	if not headless:
		await fx.warmup(cam)
	await _step()
	seed(2070)
	fx.rng.seed = 11
	var att: Array = row.get("att", ["voidsworn", "Cruiser"])
	var tgt: Array = row.get("tgt", ["deathless", "Cruiser"])
	A = _ship("A", str(att[0]), str(att[1]), Vector3(-34, 0, 0), 0)
	if A == null:
		return false
	# issue 370: a row may place the target ("tgt_at": [x, z]), for a broadside or a shot from behind
	var tat: Array = row.get("tgt_at", [34, 0])
	T = _ship("T", str(tgt[0]), str(tgt[1]), Vector3(float(tat[0]), 0, float(tat[1])), 2)
	if T == null:
		return false
	if row.has("shield_left"):
		fx.sync_ship("T", _unit(1.0, int(row["shield_left"])))
	# Issue 461: a row may park a third ship beside the target ("near": [faction, class, dx, dz] in world units from
	# the target), for example to show a torpedo hit lighting the hull next to it; and may run the engines at a level
	# ("engine": 0 to 1) instead of the parked glow, for the engine flicker rows at the close cameras.
	var near: Array = row.get("near", [])
	if near.size() >= 4:
		if _ship("N", str(near[0]), str(near[1]), T.global_position + Vector3(float(near[2]), 0.0, float(near[3])), 2) == null:
			return false
	if row.has("engine"):
		for sid in fx.ships.keys():
			fx.set_engine(str(sid), float(row["engine"]))
	var focus: Vector3 = (A if str(row.get("focus", "target")) == "attacker" else T).global_position
	# Issue 461: "attacker_engines" centres on the mean of the attacker's engine nozzles (the engine flicker rows)
	if str(row.get("focus", "")) == "attacker_engines" and fx.ship("A") != null:
		var sa = fx.ship("A")
		var sum := Vector3.ZERO
		for nz in sa.hull.nozzles:
			sum += sa.to_world(nz["p"])
		if sa.hull.nozzles.size() > 0:
			focus = sum / float(sa.hull.nozzles.size())
	# issue 560: a row may move the camera's focus off the ship's centre ("focus_off": [x, z] in world units), for a part
	# such as the aft deck turrets
	var fo: Array = row.get("focus_off", [0, 0])
	focus += Vector3(float(fo[0]), 0.0, float(fo[1]))
	_cam(focus, r)
	for k in 72:   # 1.2 s: engines up, the first damage and cut jobs done
		await _step()
	# Issue 1235 run 2: a row may land hits on the target first ("pre": [[kind, weapon, section], ...], one shot each,
	# 0.75 s apart, each on its named hull section: eng, mid or prow; Artoo on PR 1570: without it every hit took "mid")
	# and then set its hull state ("sync_t": a unit view, as the game's sync sends), for worn-ship rows; "do": "hold"
	# then shows the ship as it stands. A commit without these keys ignores them.
	# Issue 1235 recheck (Artoo on PR 1570): a pre entry may hit the shield ([kind, weapon, section, "shield"]) or be a
	# boarding party (["board"], the game's fx.board), for the list-side and boarding-then-wear rows.
	for pv in row.get("pre", []):
		if str(pv[0]) == "board":
			fx.board("A", "T")
			for k in 90:
				await _step()
			continue
		var ph: Array = _hits(1, (pv as Array).size() > 3 and str(pv[3]) == "shield", false)
		if (pv as Array).size() > 2:
			ph[0]["section"] = str(pv[2])
		fx.volley("A", str(pv[0]), "T", {"weapon_id": str(pv[1]), "shots": [true], "hits": ph})
		for k in 45:
			await _step()
	if row.get("sync_t") is Dictionary:
		fx.sync_ship("T", row["sync_t"])
		for k in 30:
			await _step()
	fx.rng.seed = 11
	seed(2070)
	var t_ev: float = fx.now
	var impacts: Array = []
	var what := str(row.get("do", "volley"))
	if what == "volley":
		var kind := str(row.get("kind", "battery"))
		var wid := str(row.get("weapon", kind))
		var n := int(row.get("shots", 0))
		if n <= 0:
			n = WEAP.default_shots(WEAP.look_of(kind, wid, str(att[0])))
		var shots := []
		for i in n:
			shots.append(true)
		var res: Dictionary = fx.volley("A", kind, "T", {"weapon_id": wid, "shots": shots, "slot": int(row.get("slot", -1)),
			"hits": _hits(n, str(row.get("on", "hull")) == "shield", bool(row.get("crit", false)))})
		impacts = res.get("impacts", [])
		if impacts.is_empty():
			_warn("%s: the volley reported no impact time; impact anchor set to fire + 0.6 s" % id)
	elif what == "break":
		# a hit first, so the bubble is up, then the collapse half a second later
		fx.volley("A", "gauss", "T", {"weapon_id": "gauss", "shots": [true], "hits": _hits(1, true, false)})
		for k in 30:
			await _step()
		t_ev = fx.now
		fx.shield_break("T", 3)
	elif what == "death":
		# issue 1586: a row may pick the small-hull archetype ("arch": 0 torch, 1 snap, 2 roll, 3 pop); a commit without
		# the archetypes ignores it
		if row.has("arch") and fx.ship("T") != null:
			fx.ship("T").set_meta("death_arch_force", int(row["arch"]))
		# and may put the Hollow Sun's well near the target ("well": [dx, dy, dz] from the target) for a tidal kill;
		# a strike craft target is a "Squadron" class (fx treats that class as a wing)
		if row.has("well"):
			var wv: Array = row["well"]
			fx.well = T.global_position + Vector3(float(wv[0]), float(wv[1]), float(wv[2]))
		_log("%s: death call at %.2f (step %d)" % [id, fx.now, steps])   # issue 1236: one line a death row
		fx.death("T", str(row.get("cause", "blast")))
		if row.has("well"):
			fx.later(fx.now + 8.0, func l_well_off() -> void: fx.well = Vector3.INF)
		if death_audio != null:
			death_audio.watch("T", T.global_position)
	# issue 370 (attach points): where a launch, the movement jets and the wounds start on the attacker's hull
	elif what == "launch":
		fx.launch("A", "T")
	elif what == "jets":
		# every movement jet ShipView fires, at once; the bench keeps ShipView's processing off, so each puff stays where
		# it started (that start is what this row shows)
		A._retro_puffs(1.0)
		A._aft_puffs(1.0)
		A._side_puffs(1.0, 1.0)
		A._couple_puffs(1.0, 1.0)
	elif what == "sync":
		# issue 1587: the event is a hull state change ("sync_ev", a unit view as the game's sync sends), for a section
		# crossing into stage 3 or 4 (the one-shot blowout); a commit without this key shows the ship unchanged
		if row.get("sync_ev") is Dictionary:
			fx.sync_ship("T", row["sync_ev"])
	elif what == "wounds":
		fx.sync_ship("A", {"hp": 25.0, "maxHp": 100.0, "burning": false, "sh": [5, 5, 5, 5],
			"sec": {"eng": {"hp": 10, "max": 100}, "mid": {"hp": 10, "max": 100}, "prow": {"hp": 10, "max": 100}}})
	var anchors := {"fire": t_ev, "event": t_ev, "impact": t_ev + (float(impacts[0]) if impacts.size() > 0 else 0.6)}
	# Issue 504: a row may fire a second volley from A at T during the event ("also": [seconds after the event, kind,
	# weapon]), for example a torpedo landing on a dying capital; the "also" anchor is that volley's first impact.
	var also: Array = row.get("also", [])
	var wins: Array = []
	var total := 0
	for wv in row.get("windows", [["impact", -0.07, 12]]):
		wins.append({"anchor": str(wv[0]), "at": float(wv[1]), "n": int(wv[2]), "got": 0, "next": -1})
		total += int(wv[2])
	var strip := Image.create_empty(cell.x * total, cell.y, false, Image.FORMAT_RGB8)
	var ci := 0
	var cells: Array = []
	var guard := 0
	var wi := 0
	while wi < wins.size() and guard < 900:
		var w: Dictionary = wins[wi]
		if w["anchor"] == "split":
			var sh = fx.ships.get("T")
			var split_t: float = float(sh.get_meta("death_split", t_ev + 1.0)) if sh != null else t_ev + 1.0
			anchors["split"] = split_t
		if also.size() >= 3 and not anchors.has("also_fired") and fx.now + 1e-4 >= t_ev + float(also[0]):
			anchors["also_fired"] = fx.now
			var ares: Dictionary = fx.volley("A", str(also[1]), "T", {"weapon_id": str(also[2]), "shots": [true], "hits": _hits(1, false, false)})
			var aimp: Array = ares.get("impacts", [])
			anchors["also"] = fx.now + (float(aimp[0]) if aimp.size() > 0 else 0.6)
			_log("%s: also volley %s at %.3f, impact at %.3f" % [id, str(also[1]), fx.now - t_ev, float(anchors["also"]) - t_ev])
		var start: float = float(anchors.get(w["anchor"], t_ev)) + float(w["at"])
		if w["anchor"] == "also" and not anchors.has("also"):
			start = INF
		var take := false
		if int(w["got"]) == 0:
			take = fx.now + 1e-4 >= start
		else:
			take = steps >= int(w["next"])
		if take:
			var img := _grab()
			if img != null:
				strip.blit_rect(_crop(img, crop, cell), Rect2i(Vector2i.ZERO, cell), Vector2i(ci * cell.x, 0))
			cells.append({"t": snappedf(fx.now - t_ev, 0.0001), "step": steps})
			ci += 1
			w["got"] = int(w["got"]) + 1
			w["next"] = steps + 2   # 30 frames a second: every second 1/60 s frame
			if int(w["got"]) >= int(w["n"]):
				wi += 1
				continue
		await _step()
		guard += 1
	if wi < wins.size():
		_warn("%s at %d: only %d of %d cells (a window never opened)" % [id, int(r), ci, total])
	if not keep:
		return true
	var name := "%s__c%d.png" % [id, int(r)]
	preload("res://tools/picture_provenance.gd").save_png(strip, d.path_join(name), preload("res://tools/picture_provenance.gd").capture_stage())
	report["stills"].append({"part": "moments", "id": id, "cam": int(r), "file": "moments/" + name, "cells": cells,
		"impacts": impacts})
	_log("%s at %d: %d cells" % [id, int(r), ci])
	return true

static func _hdist(q0: int, r0: int, q1: int, r1: int) -> int:
	var dq := q0 - q1

	var em := LS.material(true)
	edges.material_override = em
	edges.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
	add_child(edges)
	var groups := {}
	var T: Dictionary = VW.get("terrain", {})

			t = "rock"
		if EDGE_C.has(t) and index.has(k):
			if not groups.has(t):
				groups[t] = {}
			groups[t][k] = true
	for k in zone_of:
		var z := str(zone_of[k])
		if not groups.has(z):

		groups[z][k] = true
	var o = VW.get("obj")
	if o is Dictionary and str(o.get("type", "")) == "hold" and o.get("hex") is Dictionary:
		groups["hold"] = {key(o["hex"]["q"], o["hex"]["r"]): true}
	var meta = VW.get("map")
	if well_c != Vector3.INF and meta is Dictionary:
		var wq := int(meta["deadstar"]["q"])
		var wr := int(meta["deadstar"]["r"])
		groups["rim"] = {}
		groups["pull"] = {}
		for h in cells:
			var d := _hdist(h.q, h.r, wq, wr)
			if d <= 3:
				groups["rim"][key(h.q, h.r)] = true
			if d <= 5:
				groups["pull"][key(h.q, h.r)] = true
	# step 2: the natural terrain (nebula, ion storm, debris, rock) gets its own edge mesh, so look C can drop those hex
	# outlines (the gas, wrecks and rocks themselves show where they are) and the tactical grid still brings them back;
	# objective zones and the dead star's rings keep theirs

	gas_edges.material_override = em.duplicate()
	gas_edges.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF

	var st := SurfaceTool.new()
	st.begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES)
	var sg := SurfaceTool.new()
	sg.begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES)
	var n := 0
	var ng := 0
	for g in groups:
		if g == "debris" or g == "rock":
			continue   # issue 1359: solid_edges and cover_edges draw these, in Z and on hover
		if g == "neb" or g == "storm":
			ng += _edge_into(sg, groups[g], EDGE_C[g])

	edges.mesh = st.commit() if n > 0 else null
	gas_edges.mesh = sg.commit() if ng > 0 else null
	hazard_edges = MeshInstance3D.new()
	hazard_edges.name = "HazardEdges"
	hazard_edges.material_override = em.duplicate()
	hazard_edges.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
	add_child(hazard_edges)
	var sz := SurfaceTool.new()

	var nz := 0
	for g in HAZARD_EDGE:

	hazard_edges.mesh = sz.commit() if nz > 0 else null
	# Issue 1359: solid ground includes the map's set-piece holes, which are never board cells

	var cover: Dictionary = groups.get("debris", {})

# connected groups of hex keys (six neighbours)
func _patches_of(keys: Dictionary) -> Array:
	var out: Array = []
	var seen := {}
	for k0 in keys:
		if seen.has(k0): continue
		var patch := {}
		var todo: Array = [k0]
		seen[k0] = true
		while not todo.is_empty():
			var k: String = str(todo.pop_back())
			patch[k] = true
			var qr: PackedStringArray = k.split(",")
			for d in [[1, 0], [-1, 0], [0, 1], [0, -1], [1, -1], [-1, 1]]:
				var nk := key(int(qr[0]) + int(d[0]), int(qr[1]) + int(d[1]))
				if keys.has(nk) and not seen.has(nk):
					seen[nk] = true
					todo.append(nk)
		out.append(patch)
	return out

func _edge_mesh(parent: Node, nm: String, em: ShaderMaterial, keys: Dictionary, col: Color) -> MeshInstance3D:
	var mi := MeshInstance3D.new()
	mi.name = nm
	mi.set_meta("edge_kind", nm)
	mi.material_override = em.duplicate()
	mi.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
	parent.add_child(mi)
	var st := SurfaceTool.new()
	st.begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLES)
	mi.mesh = st.commit() if _edge_into(st, keys, col) > 0 else null
	return mi


# the outer edges of a set of hexes into a SurfaceTool, drawn with the shared line style (render/line_style.gd, issue
# 1374): the line sits just inside the outer hex edge and its glow band runs inward; col is the role's colour and strength
func _edge_into(st: SurfaceTool, keys: Dictionary, col: Color, y := -0.36) -> int:
	var corners: Array = []
	for i in 6:
		var an := deg_to_rad(60.0 * i + 30.0)
		corners.append(Vector3(cos(an), 0, sin(an)))
	var n := 0
	var r0 := HS * 0.97
	for k in keys:
		var qr: PackedStringArray = str(k).split(",")
		var c := hex_world(int(qr[0]), int(qr[1]), y)
		for i in 6:
			var a: Vector3 = corners[i]
			var b: Vector3 = corners[(i + 1) % 6]
			var nb := world_hex(c + (a + b) * 0.5 * HS * 2.0)
			if keys.has(key(nb.x, nb.y)):
				continue
			n += 1
			# toward the centre along the corner spokes, scaled so one unit along them is one unit in from the edge
			LS.strip_into(st, c + a * r0, c + b * r0, -a / 0.8660254, -b / 0.8660254, "edge", col)
	return n

func _terrain() -> void:
	base_fill.clear()
	rock_meshes = _rock_lib()
	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
	rng.seed = int(WI.get("seed", 1)) if WI.get("seed") != null else 1
	var T: Dictionary = VW.get("terrain", {})
	for k in T:
		var typ: String = T[k]
		var qr: PackedStringArray = k.split(",")
		var q := int(qr[0])
		var r := int(qr[1])
		var c := hex_world(q, r)
		if ZONE_TINT.has(typ):
			base_fill[k] = ZONE_TINT[typ]
		match typ:
			"rock":
				if not props_world:
					_rocks(c, rng, 3 + rng.randi() % 3, 2.5, 6.5)
			"hulk":
				_rocks(c, rng, 2, 1.5, 3.0)
				_hulk(c, rng)
			"debris":
				if not props_world:
					_rocks(c, rng, 5, 0.5, 1.4)
			"station":
				pass
	_planet()
	_beacon()
	# one station structure per cluster of station hexes (the game builds one across the cluster)
	var seen := {}
	for k in T:
		if T[k] != "station" or seen.has(k):
			continue
		var stack := [k]
		var cl: Array = []
		seen[k] = true
		while not stack.is_empty():
			var cur: String = stack.pop_back()
			cl.append(cur)
			var qr: PackedStringArray = cur.split(",")
			for d in [[1, 0], [0, 1], [-1, 1], [-1, 0], [0, -1], [1, -1]]:
				var nk := key(int(qr[0]) + d[0], int(qr[1]) + d[1])
				if T.get(nk, "") == "station" and not seen.has(nk):
					seen[nk] = true
					stack.append(nk)
		var cen := Vector3.ZERO
		var centres: Array[Vector3] = []
		for ck in cl:
			var qr2: PackedStringArray = ck.split(",")
			var p := hex_world(int(qr2[0]), int(qr2[1]))

		# still need solid docking hardware, not just an exclusion outline.
		if kind == "station" and not solid_at(get_parent(), p):
			station_fallback(self, p)

static func solid_at(node: Node3D, p: Vector3) -> bool:
	if node is MeshInstance3D and node.mesh != null:
		var bounds: AABB = node.global_transform * node.mesh.get_aabb()
		if p.x >= bounds.position.x and p.x <= bounds.end.x and p.z >= bounds.position.z and p.z <= bounds.end.z: return true
	for child in node.get_children():
		if child is Node3D and solid_at(child, p): return true
	return false

	var node := Node3D.new()
	node.name = "BlockedFootprint"
	parent.add_child(node)
	node.position = p + Vector3.UP * 0.5
	var mat := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	mat.albedo_color = col
	mat.emission_enabled = true
	mat.emission = col * 0.65
	mat.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
	mat.no_depth_test = true
	for i in 6:
		var a := Vector3(cos(PI / 6.0 + i * TAU / 6.0), 0, sin(PI / 6.0 + i * TAU / 6.0)) * 9.6
		var b := Vector3(cos(PI / 6.0 + (i + 1) * TAU / 6.0), 0, sin(PI / 6.0 + (i + 1) * TAU / 6.0)) * 9.6
		var mi := MeshInstance3D.new()
		var mesh := BoxMesh.new()
		mesh.size = Vector3(width, width * 0.6, a.distance_to(b))
		mi.mesh = mesh
		mi.material_override = mat
		node.add_child(mi)
		mi.position = (a + b) * 0.5
		# Local-space aim (Muse review #86, Opus confirmed Nov 3): look_at_from_position works in
		# global space, so inside the tree it moved every segment to near the world origin.
		mi.basis = Basis.looking_at(b - mi.position, Vector3.UP, true)
	return node

func rock_cluster(p: Vector3, kind: String, rock_kind: String, mat: Material, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Node3D:
	var node := Node3D.new()
	node.name = "Blocker_" + kind
	add_child(node)
	node.position = p
	var names := WR.names_for(rock_kind)
	var phase := rng.randf() * TAU
	# A core and six overlapping shoulders fill the hex. Bound each piece by a
	# sphere, keeping the whole cluster inside the hex's 8.66-unit inner radius.
	for i in 7:
		var mesh_name := str(names[rng.randi() % names.size()])
		var mesh := WR.mesh(mesh_name)
		var radius := rng.randf_range(5.8, 6.2) if i == 0 else rng.randf_range(3.4, 3.7)
		var angle := phase + (i - 1) * TAU / 6.0 + rng.randf_range(-0.09, 0.09)
		var off := Vector3(0, 1.8, 0) if i == 0 else Vector3(cos(angle) * 4.8, rng.randf_range(0.3, 2.2), sin(angle) * 4.8)
		var mi := cluster_piece(node, mesh, mat, off, radius, rng)
		mi.name = mesh_name
		var box := mesh.get_aabb()
		mi.set_instance_shader_parameter("rock_radius", box.position.abs().max(box.end.abs()).length())
	return node


static func cluster_piece(parent: Node3D, mesh: Mesh, mat: Material, off: Vector3, radius: float, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> MeshInstance3D:
	var mi := MeshInstance3D.new()
	mi.mesh = mesh
	mi.material_override = mat
	var box := mesh.get_aabb()
	var b := Basis(Quaternion(rng.randfn(), rng.randfn(), rng.randfn(), rng.randfn()).normalized())
	b = b.scaled(Vector3.ONE * (radius * 2.0 / maxf(box.size.length(), 0.01)))
	mi.transform = Transform3D(b, off - b * box.get_center())
	parent.add_child(mi)
	return mi


static func hulk_fallback(parent: Node3D, p: Vector3, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Node3D:
	# Also called by the board when its painted derelict is missing. Use the
	# surrounding debris field's torn plates, ribs, trusses and deck sections.
	var wreck_meshes := LIVING._shard_meshes()
	if _wreck_mat == null:
		var sh := Shader.new()
		# Solid blockers keep a fixed pose, including their shader geometry.
		sh.code = LIVING.WRECK_SHADER.replace("%NOISE%", WS.NOISE).replace("TIME *", "0.0 *")
		_wreck_mat = ShaderMaterial.new()
		_wreck_mat.shader = sh
	var n := Node3D.new()
	n.name = "SolidDerelict"
	parent.add_child(n)
	n.position = p
	var phase := rng.randf() * TAU
	for i in 9:
		var angle := phase + (i - 3) * TAU / 6.0
		var off := Vector3(rng.randf_range(-1, 1), rng.randf_range(0.5, 3.0), rng.randf_range(-1, 1)) if i < 3 else Vector3(cos(angle) * 4.7, rng.randf_range(0.0, 2.5), sin(angle) * 4.7)
		var radius := rng.randf_range(5.8, 6.6) if i < 3 else rng.randf_range(3.5, 3.8)
		cluster_piece(n, wreck_meshes[rng.randi() % wreck_meshes.size()], _wreck_mat, off, radius, rng)
	return n


static func fit_hulk(node: Node3D, centre: Vector3) -> void:
	var nodes: Array = [node]
	var bounds := AABB()
	var first := true
	while not nodes.is_empty():
		var part: Node = nodes.pop_back()
		if part is MeshInstance3D and part.mesh != null:
			var box: AABB = part.global_transform * part.mesh.get_aabb()
			bounds = box if first else bounds.merge(box)
			first = false
		for child in part.get_children(): nodes.append(child)
	if first: return
	var span := maxf(bounds.size.x, bounds.size.z)
	var factor := 14.0 / maxf(span, 0.01)
	var relative := bounds.get_center() - node.global_position
	node.scale *= factor
	node.global_position = centre + Vector3.UP * 2.0 - relative * factor
